In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis and application of a new family of atropisomereic 4-aminopridine-based nucleophiles.

the development of new atropisomerically constrained catalysts for the acylative KR of sec-alco-hols and we are currently exploring the scope of this methodology for a wide range of alcohols and acylating agents.
the design of chiral catalysts that can be used to resolve sec-alcohols in a rapid and efficient manner.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the 3,5-bis-phenyl substituted catalyst 2b has a higher selectivity than the 3,6-bis-phenylethynyl substituted catalyst 1a for the KR of sec-alcohol 3a.

the use of the new biaryl catalyst 2d in conjunction with the PPh3 additive allows rapid, room-temperature, acylative KR of several sec-alcohals at 1 mol% catalyst loading, with high enantioselectivities (e.g. 94% ee).

the use of a 1:1 mixture of PPh3 and the catalyst 1b (1 mol%) is optimal for KR of (S)-1-(n-(2-methylphenyl) ethyl alcohol at rt in less than 1 h with sO15 and O98% ee, and that the catalyst 1c is the most enantioselective atropisomere yet prepared (sO16).
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the 4-aminopridine/ PPh3 catalyst system is the most selective yet described for KR of sec-alcohol substrates.

we have shown the utility of atropisomerase 4-aminpyridine catalysts for the KR of sec-alcohol substrates and have identified a catalyst that gives high ee and high selectivity in KRs of sec-alcohos at rt.

we have shown that the atropisomerism in 4-aminophenylpyridines and 2-pyridyl-4-aminobiphenyls can be used as a means of controlling the reactivity and selectivity of these catalysts in the KR of sec-alcohol.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the combination of a nucleophilic catalyst and PPh3 can be used for rapid kinetic resolution of secalcohols at rt, which may facilitate a detailed kinetic investigation of these catalysts.
the use of atropisomerase catalysts in the kinetic resolution of racemic alcohols can provide a rapid and practical route to chiral alcohols.
atropisomerase catalysts can be made that are highly selective for the acylation of sec-alcoh.
